title: tailworks.jsonc
description: tailworks' per-app config: tailnet identity, tier, placement and public routes. Worker settings (main, bindings, vars, crons) stay in wrangler.jsonc. Reference: docs/tailworks-jsonc.md.

$schema.description: Path or URL of this schema, for editor completion.

name.description: Workload name (a DNS label). Default: wrangler.jsonc name, then the directory name.

runtime.description: "workerd" (default) or "node" for the Node process tier (docs/node-tier.md).

node.description: runtime "node" only: how the Node app is started.

listen.description: Where the app listens: "tcp" (default: PORT on 127.0.0.1) or "unix" (TW_SOCKET). "unix" keeps AF_UNIX open to the app, so a host with a reachable system tailscaled socket can't be shared with other tenants (docs/node-tier.md); prefer the default.

health.description: Health check path. Default "/": any HTTP answer there counts as up, so most apps don't need it.

tier.description: Isolation tier. Default: the tenant's. "microvm" needs a Linux host with KVM (docs/INSTALL.md).

replicas.description: Run a stateless workload on this many distinct hosts (docs/services.md). Default 1.

placement.description: Smart placement: which host runs the workload.

mode.description: Default "smart" when tailnet.connects or targets are set.

targets.description: Peers (tags or names) to place close to. Default: tailnet.connects.

host.description: Cloudflare hint: the same as targets: [host].

hostname.description: Cloudflare hint: the same as targets: [hostname].

containers.description: Container classes (docs/containers.md): wrangler's array form, or per-class image refs you pin; mgmt records the digests it resolves in the deployment.

tags.description: Tags of the workload's own node. Your policy must let tag:tw own them.

service.description: true ("svc:<workload>") or a Tailscale Service name: a stable name and VIP (docs/services.md).

https.description: Also serve the workload node on https://<name>.<tailnet>.ts.net (port 443, its ts.net certificate); requests that arrive that way see an https:// request.url. Needs HTTPS certificates on the tailnet. Plain http:// on port 80 keeps working (docs/tailworks-jsonc.md#tailnethttps).

connects.description: Declared dependencies (tags or names), optionally with the TCP port the workload dials ("tag:db:5432"; default tcp:80). tw deploy preflights these grants.

internet.description: Internet egress for Worker code and containers (docs/tailworks-jsonc.md#tailnetegressinternet). Absent: Workers may reach any public host, containers none. true: both may reach any public host. false or []: neither. A list of hosts ("*.suffix", IPs, CIDRs, each with an optional :port): both only those; an entry with a port covers that port only. TCP port 25 is refused unless an entry names it ("smtp.example.com:25"). Private, link-local, loopback and tailnet addresses are always refused.

via.description: "exit-node": run only on a host whose internet egress leaves through a tailnet exit node (docs/tailworks-jsonc.md#tailnetegressvia). Absent: whatever the host offers.

maxLive.description: The most live sub-agents (ctx.tailnet.spawn) under one root object. Default and ceiling 64: a deployment may only lower it; a larger value is lowered to 64, and 0 or absent means 64.

maxDepth.description: The deepest spawn chain. Default and ceiling 3: a deployment may only lower it; a larger value is lowered to 3, and 0 or absent means 3.

objects.description: Durable Object classes that get a tailnet node per instance, by class name (must match wrangler.jsonc durable_objects).

agent.description: Accepted and ignored (it used to mark Agents SDK classes).

ttl.description: Lifetime from creation, e.g. "10m"; the default for spawn().

node.description: false: an internal class with no tailnet node; its egress leaves as the workload node.

egress.description: "object" (default, facet mode): egress leaves from each instance's own node. "workload": plain-DO mode, egress leaves as the workload node. "node": false implies "workload"; don't set both.

fence.description: "never": instances tolerate running on two hosts, so mgmt may move it without --force-takeover.

public.description: Let public requests create objects of this class (docs/public-ingress.md).
Paths reachable from the public internet over Funnel (docs/public-ingress.md).

upgrade.description: Routes (also in routes) that may upgrade to WebSocket/SSE.

maxConnsPerIp.description: Concurrent connections per client address (IPv6: per /64).

upgradeLifetimeSeconds.description: Longest an upgraded (WebSocket) connection stays open.
